reviewer_findings: Retail availability is context, not the answer to a question about pocket contents and cabin stowage.
The 1993 report says extra clothes and some paperback books were added to expandable exterior pockets; it does not say full or overfilled.
The undated airline overhead-bin retrospective could imply a post-1993 change if placed after the 1993 test, so the beat is removed.
The museum display immediately after the 1939 lecture could imply an unproved same physical suitcase, so the visual now cuts to a separate Sadow-era family.

caveats: 1939 report records a wheeled suitcase at one study-club appearance; it does not identify the same 1928 homemade case or prove wheeled luggage at every lecture.
The 1993 report is a contemporary reporter’s own comparison; mail-order-to-retail wording does not establish exact launch dates, overall sales or universal cabin compatibility.
The 1993 report says extra clothes and paperback books went into expandable exterior pockets, making her Travelpro fail under-seat/overhead stowage until emptied. It does not say the pocket was full.

The new question concerns cabin stowage after adding those items. Retail availability and general cabin fit are context, not a payoff for that specific packing question. The loop still needs blind listening and picture anti-spoiler review.
The undated airline overhead-bin retrospective is removed from r4 narration after 1993; no chronology or causal link from the reporter test to airline modifications is asserted.
The Anita museum-case beat is removed from narration and imagery. The Midland report does not establish that its 1939 case is the surviving 1928 family object.
All prior r2 source, chronology and visual caveats remain binding; see the frozen r2 source-map and validation under base/.
